newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says can't curb rightists in isle dispute.
newsitem.headline: Japan says can't curb rightists in isle dispute.

text.p: Japan said on Friday it did not have the authority to bar right-wingers from erecting a lighthouse on an island in the East China Sea at the centre of a sovereignty dispute between Tokyo, Beijing and Taipei.
"The government does not have the authority or power to block private citizens to do such activities on privately owned property," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama said.

A long-dormant sovereignty dispute over the islands, called the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese, erupted in July after the right-wing Japan Youth Federation erected a lighthouse on one of the islands, angering Taiwan and China, which also claim ownership of the islands.

Japanese rightists sailed to the islands this week and repaired the makeshift aluminium lighthouse, which was damaged by a typhoon last month, fuelling anti-Japanese protests in Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan and mainland China.

On Thursday, a group of Hong Kong legislators urged China to send warships to guard the disputed islands, while fishermen in Taiwan hurled rotten fish at Japan's visa office there and burnt Japanese flags.
Japanese officials have said Tokyo does not support the right-wing group's activities.
Nevertheless, Kajiyama said Tokyo had no plans to compromise with the rival claimants.
"We can only pray that the issue will not escalate to a critical point," he said.
China told Tokyo on Tuesday it should not allow right-wing groups to set foot on the disputed islands and lodged a strong protest with the Japanese government.
The Japanese right-wing group said it had built the lighthouse to ensure the safety of ships sailing in the East China Sea.
Tokyo's claim to the islands dates from 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
